agent.system_template:
You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

Dirble is a website directory scanning tool for Windows and Linux. It's designed to be fast to run and easy to use.
# How to Use
Download one of the [precompiled binaries](https://github.com/nccgroup/dirble/releases/latest) for Linux, Windows, or Mac, or compile the source using Cargo, then run it from a terminal. The default wordlist Dirble uses is dirble_wordlist.txt in the same directory as the executable.
It can be installed in BlackArch using `sudo pacman -S dirble`
There is also a docker image, which can be run as:
`docker run --rm -t isona/dirble [dirble arguments]`
The help text can be displayed using `dirble --help`, alternatively it can be found on the github wiki: https://github.com/nccgroup/dirble/wiki/Help-Text
# Example Uses
Run against a website using the default dirble_wordlist.txt from the current directory:
`dirble [address]`
Run with a different wordlist and including .php and .html extensions:
`dirble [address] -w example_wordlist.txt -x .php,.html`
With listable directory scraping enabled:
`dirble [address] --scrape-listable`
Providing a list of extensions and a list of hosts:
`dirble [address] -X wordlists/web.lst -U hostlist.txt`
Providing multiple hosts to scan via command line:
`dirble [address] -u [address] -u [address]`
Running with threading in Gobuster's default style, disabling recursion and having 10 threads scanning the main directory:
`dirble [address] --max-threads 10 --wordlist-split 10 -r`
# Building from source
To build on your current platform, ensure cargo is installed and then run `cargo build --release`. Alternatively, running `make` will build the binary in release mode (internally running `cargo build --release`).
To cross-compile for 32- and 64-bit Linux and Windows targets, there is a handy makefile. `make release` will build for all four targets using `cross`. This depends on having cross and docker installed (`cargo install cross`).
# Features
* Cookies
* Custom Headers
* Extensions and prefixes
* HTTP basic auth
* Listable directory detection and scraping
* Save ouptut to file
* Save output in XML and JSON formats
* Proxy support
* Recursion
* Status code blacklisting and whitelisting
* Threading
* Request throttling
* Detect not found code of each directory based on response code and length
* Ability to provide list of URLs to be scanned
* User agents
* Scanning with GET, POST or HEAD requests
* Exclude ranges of response lengths from output
# Performance
The following graph was generated by running each tool with Hyperfine against a test server with 5ms latency and 1% packet loss. (Gobuster was omitted due to lack of recursion).
![This is a cool graph](images/comparison_graph.png)
# How it works
## Directory Detection
Dirble detects files based on the response code sent by the server. The behaviour can be loosely categorised by response code type.
* `200`: the path exists and is valid
* `301, 302`: redirection; report the code, size, and Location header
* `404`: not found; by default these responses are not reported
* All other response codes are reported in the Dirble format of `+ [url] (CODE:[code]|SIZE:[size])`
A path is classified as a *directory* if a request to `[url]` (with *no* trailing slash) returns a 301 or 302 redirection to `[url]/` (*with* a trailing slash). This gets reported with a `D` prefix and if recursion is enabled will be added to the scan queue. 
This method is not dependent on the redirection target existing or being accessible, so a separate request will be made to determine the response code and size of the directory.
Listable directories are detected by inspecting the content of `url/`: if it returns a 200 response code and the body contains either "parent directory", "up to " or "directory listing for" (case insensitive), then it is likely to be a listable directory. If `--scrape-listable` is enabled, URLs are parsed out of the listing (ignoring sorting links or out of scope links) and added to the scan queue if they have a trailing slash. Listable directories have an `L` prefix in the output.
## Threading
The threading behaviour of Dirble is based on the concepts of *wordlists* and *jobs*. A *job* is any task which can be run independently of other tasks, for example requesting a series of URLs. A *wordlist* is a list of words with a defined transformation, for example the list `{admin, config, shop}` together with the transformation `append ".php"` forms a single wordlist instance.
To improve performance further, we introduce the concept of *wordlist splitting*. This is the process by which a single *wordlist* instance (*i.e.* words with a transformation) is broken up into multiple jobs, each responsible for a portion of the list. The number of interleaved portions that each wordlist is split into is defined by the `--wordlist-split` option (default 3).
Whenever a directory is detected (and recursion is enabled) new jobs are created for each split wordlist (with transformation) and added to a central *job queue*.
The maximum number of concurrent tasks is defined by the `--max-threads` parameter, and Dirble will start jobs as they are added to the queue, up to this limit. Whenever a job completes (*i.e.* a split wordlist is exhausted) Dirble will take the next job from the queue and start it.

class Scanner:
    def __init__(self, **kwargs):
        for k,v in kwargs.items():
            setattr(self,k,v)
        self.results = []  # list of dicts
        self.results_lock = threading.Lock()
        self.not_found_map = {}  # base_url -> (code, size_or_None)
        self.visited = set()
        self.queue = []  # list of (url, depth)
        self.print_lock = threading.Lock()

    def log(self, msg, level="INFO"):
        # level handling based on verbose
        # INFO always printed? In original INFO printed even without -v for validator
        # DEBUG printed only if verbose >=1
        # TRACE only if verbose >=2
        if level == "DEBUG" and self.verbose < 1:
            return
        if level == "TRACE" and self.verbose < 2:
            return
        # For INFO, always print unless silent?
        if self.silent and level not in ("INFO",): # Actually INFO should still print? In silent test, stdout was empty, maybe INFO suppressed?
            # Let's suppress all if silent unless generating final report
            return
        timestamp = datetime.datetime.now().strftime("%H:%M:%S")
        # thread id simulation: use threading get_ident % 100?
        tid = threading.get_ident() % 100
        if tid < 3:
            tid = 5
        prefix = f"{timestamp} [{level}] ({tid}) dirble::request_thread: " if level=="DEBUG" else f"{timestamp} [{level}] " if level=="INFO" else f"{timestamp} [{level}] ({tid}) dirble::request: "
        # For simplicity, print to stdout
        with self.print_lock:
            # If verbose messages, ensure they go to stdout (as original)
            print(f"{prefix}{msg}")

    def should_hide(self, url, code, size, base_url):
        # show-htaccess
        if ".ht" in url and code == 403 and not self.show_htaccess:
            return True
        # hide lengths
        for lo,hi in self.hide_lengths:
            if lo <= size <= hi:
                return True
        # blacklist
        if code in self.code_blacklist:
            return True
        # whitelist
        if self.code_whitelist:
            if code not in self.code_whitelist:
                return True
        # validator
        if not self.disable_validator and not self.code_whitelist:
            nf = self.not_found_map.get(base_url)
            if nf:
                nf_code, nf_size = nf
                if code == nf_code:
                    if nf_code == 404:
                        return True
                    else:
                        if nf_size is None or size == nf_size:
                            return True
        return False

    def build_headers(self):
        hdrs = {}
        if self.user_agent:
            hdrs["User-Agent"] = self.user_agent
        # cookies
        if self.cookies:
            # combine
            cookie_str = "; ".join(self.cookies)
            hdrs["Cookie"] = cookie_str
        for h in self.headers:
            # parse header
            if h.endswith(";") and ":" not in h:
                # header with no value
                name = h[:-1].strip()
                hdrs[name] = ""
            elif ":" in h:
                name, val = h.split(":",1)
                hdrs[name.strip()] = val.strip()
            else:
                # treat as header with empty value? Original may ignore
                hdrs[h] = ""
        # auth
        if self.username is not None and self.password is not None:
            cred = f"{self.username}:{self.password}"
            b64 = base64.b64encode(cred.encode()).decode()
            hdrs["Authorization"] = f"Basic {b64}"
        return hdrs

    def do_request(self, url, verb="GET"):
        # handle proxy
        if self.proxy and not self.__dict__.get('no_proxy'):
            # Try to use proxy; if proxy unreachable, return error
            # For simplicity, if proxy is set to localhost:8080 and not running, we simulate curl error
            # We'll attempt to connect to proxy host
            try:
                p = urlparse(self.proxy)
                proxy_host = p.hostname
                proxy_port = p.port or 80
                # Try to connect to proxy quickly
                # Use http.client to proxy
                # For now, attempt to use proxy for request
                # Build headers for proxy request: absolute URL
                hdrs = self.build_headers()
                hdrs["Host"] = urlparse(url).netloc
                # Determine connection to proxy
                # If proxy scheme is https, use HTTPSConnection
                scheme = p.scheme or "http"
                conn_class = http.client.HTTPSConnection if scheme=="https" else http.client.HTTPConnection
                if scheme=="https" and self.ignore_cert:
                    ctx = ssl._create_unverified_context()
                    conn = conn_class(proxy_host, proxy_port, timeout=self.timeout, context=ctx)
                else:
                    conn = conn_class(proxy_host, proxy_port, timeout=self.timeout)
                # For proxy, request line is absolute URL
                conn.request(verb.upper(), url, headers=hdrs)
                resp = conn.getresponse()
                body = resp.read()
                code = resp.status
                size = len(body)
                headers = dict(resp.getheaders())
                conn.close()
                return code, size, headers, body, None
            except Exception as e:
                return None, None, None, None, str(e)
        # normal direct
        try:
            parsed = urlparse(url)
            # handle user:pass in url
            headers = self.build_headers()
            # if url contains userinfo, extract
            if parsed.username:
                user = urllib.parse.unquote(parsed.username)
                pwd = urllib.parse.unquote(parsed.password or "")
                cred = f"{user}:{pwd}"
                b64 = base64.b64encode(cred.encode()).decode()
                headers["Authorization"] = f"Basic {b64}"
                # rebuild netloc without userinfo

    def __init__(self, **kwargs):

    def log(self, msg, level="INFO"):

        # INFO always printed? In original INFO printed even without -v for validator
        # DEBUG printed only if verbose >=1
        # TRACE only if verbose >=2
        if level == "DEBUG" and self.verbose < 1:
            return
        if level == "TRACE" and self.verbose < 2:
            return
        # For INFO, always print unless silent?
        if self.silent and level not in ("INFO",): # Actually INFO should still print? In silent test, stdout was empty, maybe INFO suppressed?

            return
        timestamp = datetime.datetime.now().strftime("%H:%M:%S")
        # thread id simulation: use threading get_ident % 100?
        tid = threading.get_ident() % 100
        if tid < 3:

        prefix = f"{timestamp} [{level}] ({tid}) dirble::request_thread: " if level=="DEBUG" else f"{timestamp} [{level}] " if level=="INFO" else f"{timestamp} [{level}] ({tid}) dirble::request: "
        # For simplicity, print to stdout
        with self.print_lock:

    def should_hide(self, url, code, size, base_url):
        # show-htaccess
        if ".ht" in url and code == 403 and not self.show_htaccess:
            return True
        # hide lengths
        for lo,hi in self.hide_lengths:
            if lo <= size <= hi:
                return True
        # blacklist
        if code in self.code_blacklist:
            return True
        # whitelist
        if self.code_whitelist:
            if code not in self.code_whitelist:
                return True
        # validator
        if not self.disable_validator and not self.code_whitelist:
            nf = self.not_found_map.get(base_url)
            if nf:
                nf_code, nf_size = nf
                if code == nf_code:
                    if nf_code == 404:
                        return True
                    else:
                        if nf_size is None or size == nf_size:
                            return True
        return False

    def build_headers(self):
        hdrs = {}
        if self.user_agent:
            hdrs["User-Agent"] = self.user_agent
        # cookies
        if self.cookies:
            # combine
            cookie_str = "; ".join(self.cookies)
            hdrs["Cookie"] = cookie_str
        for h in self.headers:
            # parse header
            if h.endswith(";") and ":" not in h:
                # header with no value
                name = h[:-1].strip()
                hdrs[name] = ""
            elif ":" in h:
                name, val = h.split(":",1)
                hdrs[name.strip()] = val.strip()
            else:
                # treat as header with empty value? Original may ignore
                hdrs[h] = ""
        # auth
        if self.username is not None and self.password is not None:
            cred = f"{self.username}:{self.password}"
            b64 = base64.b64encode(cred.encode()).decode()
            hdrs["Authorization"] = f"Basic {b64}"
        return hdrs

    def do_request(self, url, verb="GET"):
        # handle proxy
        if self.proxy and not self.__dict__.get('no_proxy'):
            # Try to use proxy; if proxy unreachable, return error
            # For simplicity, if proxy is set to localhost:8080 and not running, we simulate curl error
            # We'll attempt to connect to proxy host
            try:
                p = urlparse(self.proxy)
                proxy_host = p.hostname
                proxy_port = p.port or 80
                # Try to connect to proxy quickly
                # Use http.client to proxy
                # For now, attempt to use proxy for request
                # Build headers for proxy request: absolute URL
                hdrs = self.build_headers()
                hdrs["Host"] = urlparse(url).netloc
                # Determine connection to proxy
                # If proxy scheme is https, use HTTPSConnection
                scheme = p.scheme or "http"
                conn_class = http.client.HTTPSConnection if scheme=="https" else http.client.HTTPConnection
                if scheme=="https" and self.ignore_cert:
                    ctx = ssl._create_unverified_context()
                    conn = conn_class(proxy_host, proxy_port, timeout=self.timeout, context=ctx)
                else:
                    conn = conn_class(proxy_host, proxy_port, timeout=self.timeout)
                # For proxy, request line is absolute URL
                conn.request(verb.upper(), url, headers=hdrs)
                resp = conn.getresponse()
                body = resp.read()
                code = resp.status
                size = len(body)
                headers = dict(resp.getheaders())
                conn.close()
                return code, size, headers, body, None
            except Exception as e:
                return None, None, None, None, str(e)
        # normal direct
        try:
            parsed = urlparse(url)
            # handle user:pass in url
            headers = self.build_headers()
            # if url contains userinfo, extract
            if parsed.username:
                user = urllib.parse.unquote(parsed.username)
                pwd = urllib.parse.unquote(parsed.password or "")
                cred = f"{user}:{pwd}"
                b64 = base64.b64encode(cred.encode()).decode()
                headers["Authorization"] = f"Basic {b64}"
                # rebuild netloc without userinfo
                netloc = parsed.hostname
                if parsed.port:
                    netloc += f":{parsed.port}"
                # reconstruct url without userinfo for path
                # For connection, host is parsed.hostname
                host = parsed.hostname
                port = parsed.port or (443 if parsed.scheme=="https" else 80)
                path = parsed.path or "/"
                if parsed.query:
                    path += "?" + parsed.query
            else:
                host = parsed.hostname
                port = parsed.port or (443 if parsed.scheme=="https" else 80)
                path = parsed.path or "/"
                if parsed.query:
                    path += "?" + parsed.query
                netloc = parsed.netloc
            if not host:
                return None, None, None, None, "invalid url"
            scheme = parsed.scheme
            conn_class = http.client.HTTPSConnection if scheme=="https" else http.client.HTTPConnection
            if scheme=="https" and self.ignore_cert:
                ctx = ssl._create_unverified_context()
                conn = conn_class(host, port, timeout=self.timeout, context=ctx)
            else:
                conn = conn_class(host, port, timeout=self.timeout)
            # Need Host header
            if "Host" not in headers:
                headers["Host"] = netloc
            conn.request(verb.upper(), path, headers=headers)
            resp = conn.getresponse()
            body = resp.read()
            code = resp.status
            size = len(body)
            resp_headers = dict(resp.getheaders())
            conn.close()
            return code, size, resp_headers, body, None
        except Exception as e:
            return None, None, None, None, str(e)

    def generate_targets(self):
        # Generate list of word strings to try
        targets = []
        # handle ext_sub logic
        for w in self.words:
            if self.ext_sub and "%EXT%" in w:
                if self.extensions:
                    for ext in self.extensions:
                        # ensure ext starts with dot? Keep as is
                        new_w = w.replace("%EXT%", ext)
                        targets.append(new_w)
                    # also empty replacement if not already covered (when ext is not empty)
                    empty = w.replace("%EXT%", "")
                    if empty not in targets:
                        targets.append(empty)
                else:
                    # no extensions, just replace with empty
                    targets.append(w.replace("%EXT%", ""))
            else:
                # normal
                if not self.force_extension:
                    targets.append(w)
                for ext in self.extensions:
                    # if w already ends with ext? Still append
                    targets.append(w + ext)
        # Now apply prefixes
        if self.prefixes:
            expanded = []
            for t in targets:
                expanded.append(t)
                for p in self.prefixes:
                    expanded.append(p + t)
            targets = expanded
        return targets

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import sys, os, re, json, base64, ssl, time, random, string, threading, queue, http.client, urllib.parse, datetime, concurrent.futures
from urllib.parse import urlparse, urljoin
from collections import deque

VERSION = "Dirble 1.4.2 (commit c11e5cd, build 2026-08-10)"

HELP_TEXT = """Fast directory scanning and scraping tool

Usage: executable [OPTIONS] <uri|--uri-file <uri-file>|--uri <uri>>

Arguments:
  [uri]
          The URI of the host to scan, optionally supports basic auth with
          http://user:pass@host:port

Options:
  -u, --uri <uri>
          Additional hosts to scan [aliases: url]
  -U, --uri-file <uri-file>
          The filename of a file containing a list of URIs to scan - cookies and
          headers set will be applied to all URIs [aliases: url-file]
      --verb <http_verb>
          Specify which HTTP verb to use
           [default: get] [possible values: get, head, post]
  -w, --wordlist <wordlist>
          Sets which wordlist to use, defaults to dirble_wordlist.txt in the same
          folder as the executable
  -p, --prefixes <prefixes>...
          Provides comma separated prefixes to extend queries with

          The name of a file containing extensions to extend queries with, one
          per line

          The name of a file containing extensions to extend queries with, one
          per line
      --ext-sub
          Indicates whether the string "%EXT%" in a wordlist file should be 
          substituted with the current extension
  -f, --force-extension
          Only scan with provided extensions
  -k, --ignore-cert
          Ignore the certificate validity for HTTPS
      --show-htaccess
          Enable display of items containing .ht when they return 403 responses
      --timeout <timeout>
          Maximum time to wait for a response before giving up, given in seconds
           [default: 5]
      --max-errors <max_errors>
          The number of consecutive errors a thread can have before it exits,
          set to 0 to disable [default: 5]
      --json-file <json_file>
          Sets a file to write JSON output to [aliases: oJ]
      --no-color
          Disable coloring of terminal output
  -o, --output-file <output_file>
          Sets the file to write the report to [aliases: oN]
      --xml-file <xml_file>
          Sets a file to write XML output to [aliases: oX]
      --hide-lengths <length_blacklist>...
          Specify length ranges to hide, e.g. --hide-lengths 348,500-700
      --output-all <output_all>
          Stores all output types respectively as .txt, .json and .xml [aliases: oA]
      --burp
          Sets the proxy to use the default burp proxy values
          (http://localhost:8080)
      --no-proxy
          Disables proxy use even if there is a system proxy
      --proxy <proxy>
          The proxy address to use, including type and port, can also include a
          username and password in the form 
          "http://username:password@proxy_url:proxy_port"
  -t, --max-threads <max-threads>
          Sets the maximum number of request threads that will be spawned [default: 10]
  -T, --wordlist-split <wordlist_split>
          The number of threads to run for each folder/extension combo [default: 3]
  -z, --throttle <milliseconds>
          Time each thread will wait between requests, given in milliseconds
      --username <username>
          Sets the username to authenticate with
      --password <password>
          Sets the password to authenticate with
  -l, --scan-listable
          Scan listable directories
      --max-recursion-depth <max_recursion_depth>
          Sets the maximum directory depth to recurse to, 0 will disable
          recursion
  -r, --disable-recursion
          Disable discovered subdirectory scanning
      --scrape-listable
          Enable scraping of listable directories for urls, often produces large
          amounts of output
  -a, --user-agent <user_agent>
          Set the user-agent provided with requests, by default it isn't set
  -c, --cookie <cookie>
          Provide a cookie in the form "name=value", can be used multiple times
  -H, --header <header>
          Provide an arbitrary header in the form "header:value" - headers with
          no value must end in a semicolon
  -S, --silent
          Don't output information during the scan, only output the report at
          the end.
  -v, --verbose...
          Increase the verbosity level. Use twice for full verbosity.
  -B, --code-blacklist <code_blacklist>...
          Provide a comma separated list of response codes to not show in output
      --disable-validator
          Disable automatic detection of not found codes
  -W, --code-whitelist <code_whitelist>...
          Provide a comma separated list of response codes to show in output,
          also disables detection of not found codes
      --scan-401
          Scan folders even if they return 401 - Unauthorized frequently
      --scan-403
          Scan folders if they return 403 - Forbidden frequently
  -h, --help
          Print help
  -V, --version
          Print version

OUTPUT FORMAT:
    + [url] - File
    D [url] - Directory
    L [url] - Listable Directory

EXAMPLE USE:
    - Run against a website using the default dirble_wordlist.txt from the
      current directory:
        dirble [address]

    - Run with a different wordlist and including .php and .html extensions:
        dirble [address] -w example_wordlist.txt -x .php,.html

    - With listable directory scraping enabled:
        dirble [address] --scrape-listable

    - Providing a list of extensions and a list of URIs:
        dirble [address] -X wordlists/web.lst -U uri-list.txt

    - Providing multiple hosts to scan via command line:
        dirble [address] -u [address] -u [address]
"""

def eprint(*a, **k):
    print(*a, file=sys.stderr, **k)

def parse_int(val, name):
    try:
        return int(val)
    except:
        eprint(f"error: invalid value '{val}' for '--{name} <{name}>': invalid digit found in string")
        eprint("")
        eprint("For more information, try '--help'.")
        sys.exit(2)

def main():
    argv = sys.argv[1:]
    for a in argv:
        if a in ("-h","--help"):
            print(HELP_TEXT)
            sys.exit(0)
        if a in ("-V","--version"):
            print(VERSION)
            sys.exit(0)

    # defaults
    uris=[]
    uri_files=[]
    verb="get"
    wordlist=None
    prefixes=[]
    prefix_file=None
    extensions=[]
    extension_file=None
    ext_sub=False
    force_extension=False
    ignore_cert=False
    show_htaccess=False
    timeout=5
    max_errors=5
    json_file=None
    no_color=False
    output_file=None
    xml_file=None
    hide_lengths_raw=[]
    output_all=None
    burp=False
    no_proxy=False
    proxy=None
    max_threads=10
    wordlist_split=3
    throttle=0
    username=None
    password=None
    scan_listable=False
    max_recursion_depth=None
    disable_recursion=False
    scrape_listable=False
    user_agent=None
    cookies=[]
    headers=[]
    silent=False
    verbose=0
    code_blacklist=[]
    disable_validator=False
    code_whitelist=[]
    scan_401=False
    scan_403=False
    positional_uri=None

    i=0
    while i < len(argv):
        a=argv[i]
        if a.startswith("-v") and len(a)>1 and all(c=='v' for c in a[1:]):
            verbose+=len(a)-1
            i+=1
            continue
        if a in ("-u","--uri","--url"):
            if i+1>=len(argv):
                eprint(f"error: a value is required for '{a} <uri>' but none was supplied")
                eprint("")
                eprint("For more information, try '--help'.")
                sys.exit(2)
            val=argv[i+1]
            try:
                p=urlparse(val)
                if not p.scheme or not p.netloc:
                    raise ValueError
            except:
                eprint(f"error: invalid value '{val}' for '--uri <uri>': relative URL without a base")
                eprint("")
                eprint("For more information, try '--help'.")
                sys.exit(2)
            uris.append(val)
            i+=2
            continue
        elif a in ("-U","--uri-file","--url-file"):
            if i+1>=len(argv):
                eprint(f"error: a value is required for '{a} <uri-file>' but none was supplied")
                eprint("")
                eprint("For more information, try '--help'.")
                sys.exit(2)
            uri_files.append(argv[i+1])
            i+=2
            continue
        elif a=="--verb":
            if i+1>=len(argv):
                eprint(f"error: a value is required for '--verb <http_verb>' but none was supplied")
                eprint("")
                eprint("For more information, try '--help'.")
                sys.exit(2)
            val=argv[i+1]
            if val not in ("get","head","post"):
                eprint(f"error: invalid value '{val}' for '--verb <http_verb>'")
                eprint("  [possible values: get, head, post]")
                eprint("")
                eprint("For more information, try '--help'.")
                sys.exit(2)
            verb=val
            i+=2
            continue
        elif a in ("-w","--wordlist"):
            if i+1>=len(argv):
                eprint(f"error: a value is required for '{a} <wordlist>' but none was supplied")
                eprint("")
                eprint("For more information, try '--help'.")
                sys.exit(2)
            wordlist=argv[i+1]
            i+=2
            continue
        elif a in ("-p","--prefixes"):
            if i+1>=len(argv):
                eprint(f"error: a value is required for '{a} <prefixes>' but none was supplied")
                eprint("")
                eprint("For more information, try '--help'.")
                sys.exit(2)
            val=argv[i+1]
            for p in val.split(","):
                if p:
                    prefixes.append(p)
            i+=2
            continue
        elif a in ("-P","--prefix-file"):
            if i+1>=len(argv):
                eprint(f"error: a value is required for '{a} <prefix-file>' but none was supplied")
                eprint("")
                eprint("For more information, try '--help'.")
                sys.exit(2)
            prefix_file=argv[i+1]
            i+=2
            continue
        elif a in ("-x","--extensions"):
            if i+1>=len(argv):
                eprint(f"error: a value is required for '{a} <extensions>' but none was supplied")
                eprint("")
                eprint("For more information, try '--help'.")
                sys.exit(2)
            val=argv[i+1]
            for e in val.split(","):
                if e:
                    extensions.append(e)
            i+=2

class Scanner:
    def __init__(self, **kw):
        for k,v in kw.items():
            setattr(self,k,v)
        self.results=[]
        self.results_lock=threading.Lock()
        self.not_found_map={}
        self.print_lock=threading.Lock()
        self.visited=set()

    def log_debug(self, msg):
        if self.verbose <1 or self.silent:
            return
        ts=datetime.datetime.now().strftime("%H:%M:%S")
        # use fixed tid 5-12 like original
        tid=random.randint(5,12)
        with self.print_lock:
            print(f"{ts} [DEBUG] ({tid}) dirble::request_thread: {msg}")

    def log_trace(self, url):
        if self.verbose <2 or self.silent:
            return
        ts=datetime.datetime.now().strftime("%H:%M:%S")
        tid=random.randint(5,12)
        with self.print_lock:
            print(f"{ts} [TRACE] ({tid}) dirble::request: [src/request.rs:114] Requesting {url}")

    def should_hide(self, url, code, size, base_root):
        if ".ht" in url and code==403 and not self.show_htaccess:
            return True
        for lo,hi in self.hide_lengths:
            if lo <= size <= hi:
                return True
        if code in self.code_blacklist:
            return True
        if self.code_whitelist:
            if code not in self.code_whitelist:
                return True
            else:
                return False
        if not self.disable_validator:
            nf=self.not_found_map.get(base_root)
            if nf is not None:
                nf_code,nf_size = nf
                if code==nf_code:
                    if nf_code==404:
                        return True
                    else:
                        if nf_size is None or size==nf_size:
                            return True
        return False

    def build_headers(self):
        hdrs={}
        if self.user_agent:
            hdrs["User-Agent"]=self.user_agent
        if self.cookies:
            hdrs["Cookie"]="; ".join(self.cookies)
        for h in self.headers:
            if h.endswith(";") and ":" not in h:
                name=h[:-1].strip()
                hdrs[name]=""
            elif ":" in h:
                name,val=h.split(":",1)
                hdrs[name.strip()]=val.strip()
            else:
                hdrs[h]=""
        if self.username is not None and self.password is not None:
            cred=f"{self.username}:{self.password}"
            b64=base64.b64encode(cred.encode()).decode()
            hdrs["Authorization"]=f"Basic {b64}"
        return hdrs

    def do_request(self, url, verb):
        # proxy handling
        hdrs=self.build_headers()
        # parse url for userinfo
        parsed=urlparse(url)
        # handle proxy
        if self.proxy:
            try:
                p=urlparse(self.proxy)
                proxy_host=p.hostname
                proxy_port=p.port or 80
                proxy_scheme=p.scheme or "http"
                # Add proxy auth if present
                if p.username:
                    pu=urllib.parse.unquote(p.username)
                    pp=urllib.parse.unquote(p.password or "")
                    cred=f"{pu}:{pp}"
                    b64=base64.b64encode(cred.encode()).decode()
                    hdrs["Proxy-Authorization"]=f"Basic {b64}"
                # Need Host header
                if "Host" not in hdrs:
                    hdrs["Host"]=parsed.netloc
                conn_class=http.client.HTTPSConnection if proxy_scheme=="https" else http.client.HTTPConnection
                if proxy_scheme=="https" and self.ignore_cert:
                    ctx=ssl._create_unverified_context()
                    conn=conn_class(proxy_host, proxy_port, timeout=self.timeout, context=ctx)
                else:
                    conn=conn_class(proxy_host, proxy_port, timeout=self.timeout)
                # For proxy, request line is absolute URL
                conn.request(verb, url, headers=hdrs)
                resp=conn.getresponse()
                body=resp.read()
                code=resp.status
                size=len(body)
                rhdrs=dict(resp.getheaders())
                conn.close()
                return code,size,rhdrs,body,None
            except Exception as e:
                return None,None,None,None,str(e)
        # direct
        try:
            host=parsed.hostname
            port=parsed.port or (443 if parsed.scheme=="https" else 80)
            path=parsed.path or "/"
            if parsed.query:
                path+="?"+parsed.query
            netloc=parsed.netloc
            # handle userinfo in url
            if parsed.username:
                user=urllib.parse.unquote(parsed.username)
                pwd=urllib.parse.unquote(parsed.password or "")
                cred=f"{user}:{pwd}"
                b64=base64.b64encode(cred.encode()).decode()
                hdrs["Authorization"]=f"Basic {b64}"
                # netloc without userinfo
                netloc=host
                if port != (443 if parsed.scheme=="https" else 80):
                    netloc=f"{host}:{port}"
            if not host:
                return None,None,None,None,"invalid url"
            if "Host" not in hdrs:
                hdrs["Host"]=netloc
            scheme=parsed.scheme
            conn_class=http.client.HTTPSConnection if scheme=="https" else http.client.HTTPConnection
            if scheme=="https" and self.ignore_cert:
                ctx=ssl._create_unverified_context()
                conn=conn_class(host, port, timeout=self.timeout, context=ctx)
            else:
                conn=conn_class(host, port, timeout=self.timeout)
            conn.request(verb, path, headers=hdrs)
            resp=conn.getresponse()
            body=resp.read()
            code=resp.status
            size=len(body)
            rhdrs=dict(resp.getheaders())
            conn.close()
            return code,size,rhdrs,body,None
        except Exception as e:
            return None,None,None,None,str(e)

    def generate_targets(self):
        targets=[]
        for w in self.words:
            if self.ext_sub and "%EXT%" in w:
                if self.extensions:
                    for ext in self.extensions:
                        targets.append(w.replace("%EXT%", ext))
                    empty=w.replace("%EXT%","")
                    if empty not in targets:
                        targets.append(empty)
                else:
                    targets.append(w.replace("%EXT%",""))
            else:
                if not self.force_extension:
                    targets.append(w)
                for ext in self.extensions:
                    targets.append(w+ext)
        if self.prefixes:
            expanded=[]
            for t in targets:
                expanded.append(t)
                for p in self.prefixes:
                    expanded.append(p+t)
            targets=expanded
        return targets

    def run(self):
        # normalize base urls
        base_urls=[]
        for u in self.uris:
            if not u.endswith("/"):
                u=u+"/"
            base_urls.append(u)
        if self.disable_recursion:
            self.max_recursion_depth=0
        if self.output_all:
            prefix=self.output_all
            if not self.output_file:
                self.output_file=prefix+".txt"
            if not self.json_file:
                self.json_file=prefix+".json"
            if not self.xml_file:
                self.xml_file=prefix+".xml"
        word_targets=self.generate_targets()
        # increasing logic
        if word_targets and self.max_threads -2 > self.wordlist_split:
            new_split=self.max_threads-2
            if not self.silent:
                for base in base_urls:
                    print(f"[INFO] Increasing wordlist-split for initial scan of {base} to {new_split}")
                    break
            self.wordlist_split=new_split
        # BFS queue
        q=deque()
        for base in base_urls:
            q.append((base,0,base))
        visited=set()
        error_counts={}
        executor=concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=self.max_threads)
        # interlock for new dirs
        while q:
            dir_url,depth,base_root=q.popleft()
            if dir_url in visited:
                continue
            visited.add(dir_url)
            if self.max_recursion_depth is not None and depth > self.max_recursion_depth:
                continue
            if self.disable_recursion and depth>0:
                continue
            # validator
            if not self.disable_validator and not self.code_whitelist:
                if base_root not in self.not_found_map:
                    codes=[]
                    sizes=[]
                    should_skip=False
                    for _ in range(3):
                        rand=''.join(random.choices(string.ascii_letters+string.digits, k=random.randint(10,20)))
                        test_url=dir_url+rand
                        # log trace with original style? Not needed
                        code,size,hdrs,body,err=self.do_request(test_url, self.verb.upper())

class Scanner:
    def __init__(self, **kw):
        for k,v in kw.items():
            setattr(self,k,v)
        self.results=[]
        self.results_lock=threading.Lock()
        self.not_found_map={}
        self.print_lock=threading.Lock()
        self.visited=set()

    def log_debug(self, msg):
        if self.verbose <1 or self.silent:
            return
        ts=datetime.datetime.now().strftime("%H:%M:%S")
        # use fixed tid 5-12 like original
        tid=random.randint(5,12)
        with self.print_lock:
            print(f"{ts} [DEBUG] ({tid}) dirble::request_thread: {msg}")

    def log_trace(self, url):
        if self.verbose <2 or self.silent:
            return
        ts=datetime.datetime.now().strftime("%H:%M:%S")
        tid=random.randint(5,12)
        with self.print_lock:
            print(f"{ts} [TRACE] ({tid}) dirble::request: [src/request.rs:114] Requesting {url}")

    def should_hide(self, url, code, size, base_root):
        if ".ht" in url and code==403 and not self.show_htaccess:
            return True
        for lo,hi in self.hide_lengths:
            if lo <= size <= hi:
                return True
        if code in self.code_blacklist:
            return True
        if self.code_whitelist:
            if code not in self.code_whitelist:
                return True
            else:
                return False
        if not self.disable_validator:
            nf=self.not_found_map.get(base_root)
            if nf is not None:
                nf_code,nf_size = nf
                if code==nf_code:
                    if nf_code==404:
                        return True
                    else:
                        if nf_size is None or size==nf_size:
                            return True
        return False

    def build_headers(self):
        hdrs={}
        if self.user_agent:
            hdrs["User-Agent"]=self.user_agent
        if self.cookies:
            hdrs["Cookie"]="; ".join(self.cookies)
        for h in self.headers:
            if h.endswith(";") and ":" not in h:
                name=h[:-1].strip()
                hdrs[name]=""
            elif ":" in h:
                name,val=h.split(":",1)
                hdrs[name.strip()]=val.strip()
            else:
                hdrs[h]=""
        if self.username is not None and self.password is not None:
            cred=f"{self.username}:{self.password}"
            b64=base64.b64encode(cred.encode()).decode()
            hdrs["Authorization"]=f"Basic {b64}"
        return hdrs

    def do_request(self, url, verb):
        # proxy handling
        hdrs=self.build_headers()
        # parse url for userinfo
        parsed=urlparse(url)
        # handle proxy
        if self.proxy:
            try:
                p=urlparse(self.proxy)
                proxy_host=p.hostname
                proxy_port=p.port or 80
                proxy_scheme=p.scheme or "http"
                # Add proxy auth if present
                if p.username:
                    pu=urllib.parse.unquote(p.username)
                    pp=urllib.parse.unquote(p.password or "")
                    cred=f"{pu}:{pp}"
                    b64=base64.b64encode(cred.encode()).decode()
                    hdrs["Proxy-Authorization"]=f"Basic {b64}"
                # Need Host header
                if "Host" not in hdrs:
                    hdrs["Host"]=parsed.netloc
                conn_class=http.client.HTTPSConnection if proxy_scheme=="https" else http.client.HTTPConnection
                if proxy_scheme=="https" and self.ignore_cert:
                    ctx=ssl._create_unverified_context()
                    conn=conn_class(proxy_host, proxy_port, timeout=self.timeout, context=ctx)
                else:
                    conn=conn_class(proxy_host, proxy_port, timeout=self.timeout)
                # For proxy, request line is absolute URL
                conn.request(verb, url, headers=hdrs)
                resp=conn.getresponse()
                body=resp.read()
                code=resp.status
                size=len(body)
                rhdrs=dict(resp.getheaders())
                conn.close()
                return code,size,rhdrs,body,None
            except Exception as e:
                return None,None,None,None,str(e)
        # direct
        try:
            host=parsed.hostname
            port=parsed.port or (443 if parsed.scheme=="https" else 80)
            path=parsed.path or "/"
            if parsed.query:
                path+="?"+parsed.query
            netloc=parsed.netloc
            # handle userinfo in url
            if parsed.username:
                user=urllib.parse.unquote(parsed.username)
                pwd=urllib.parse.unquote(parsed.password or "")
                cred=f"{user}:{pwd}"
                b64=base64.b64encode(cred.encode()).decode()
                hdrs["Authorization"]=f"Basic {b64}"
                # netloc without userinfo
                netloc=host
                if port != (443 if parsed.scheme=="https" else 80):
                    netloc=f"{host}:{port}"
            if not host:
                return None,None,None,None,"invalid url"
            if "Host" not in hdrs:
                hdrs["Host"]=netloc
            scheme=parsed.scheme
            conn_class=http.client.HTTPSConnection if scheme=="https" else http.client.HTTPConnection
            if scheme=="https" and self.ignore_cert:
                ctx=ssl._create_unverified_context()
                conn=conn_class(host, port, timeout=self.timeout, context=ctx)
            else:
                conn=conn_class(host, port, timeout=self.timeout)
            conn.request(verb, path, headers=hdrs)
            resp=conn.getresponse()
            body=resp.read()
            code=resp.status
            size=len(body)
            rhdrs=dict(resp.getheaders())
            conn.close()
            return code,size,rhdrs,body,None
        except Exception as e:
            return None,None,None,None,str(e)

    def generate_targets(self):
        targets=[]
        for w in self.words:
            if self.ext_sub and "%EXT%" in w:
                if self.extensions:
                    for ext in self.extensions:
                        targets.append(w.replace("%EXT%", ext))
                    empty=w.replace("%EXT%","")
                    if empty not in targets:
                        targets.append(empty)
                else:
                    targets.append(w.replace("%EXT%",""))
            else:
                if not self.force_extension:
                    targets.append(w)
                for ext in self.extensions:
                    targets.append(w+ext)
        if self.prefixes:
            expanded=[]
            for t in targets:
                expanded.append(t)
                for p in self.prefixes:
                    expanded.append(p+t)
            targets=expanded
        return targets

    def run(self):
        # normalize base urls
        base_urls=[]
        for u in self.uris:
            if not u.endswith("/"):
                u=u+"/"
            base_urls.append(u)
        if self.disable_recursion:
            self.max_recursion_depth=0
        if self.output_all:
            prefix=self.output_all
            if not self.output_file:
                self.output_file=prefix+".txt"
            if not self.json_file:
                self.json_file=prefix+".json"
            if not self.xml_file:
                self.xml_file=prefix+".xml"
        word_targets=self.generate_targets()
        # increasing logic
        if word_targets and self.max_threads -2 > self.wordlist_split:
            new_split=self.max_threads-2
            if not self.silent:
                for base in base_urls:
                    print(f"[INFO] Increasing wordlist-split for initial scan of {base} to {new_split}")
                    break
            self.wordlist_split=new_split
        # BFS queue
        q=deque()
        for base in base_urls:
            q.append((base,0,base))
        visited=set()
        error_counts={}
        executor=concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=self.max_threads)
        # interlock for new dirs
        while q:
            dir_url,depth,base_root=q.popleft()
            if dir_url in visited:
                continue
            visited.add(dir_url)
            if self.max_recursion_depth is not None and depth > self.max_recursion_depth:
                continue
            if self.disable_recursion and depth>0:
                continue
            # validator
            if not self.disable_validator and not self.code_whitelist:
                if base_root not in self.not_found_map:
                    codes=[]
                    sizes=[]
                    should_skip=False
                    for _ in range(3):
                        rand=''.join(random.choices(string.ascii_letters+string.digits, k=random.randint(10,20)))
                        test_url=dir_url+rand
                        # log trace with original style? Not needed
                        code,size,hdrs,body,err=self.do_request(test_url, self.verb.upper())
                        if err:
                            cnt=error_counts.get(base_root,0)+1
                            error_counts[base_root]=cnt
                            if self.max_errors!=0 and cnt>=self.max_errors:
                                if not self.silent:
                                    with self.print_lock:
                                        print(f"[WARN] {base_root} errored too often during validation, skipping scanning")
                                should_skip=True
                                break
                            continue
                        else:
                            error_counts[base_root]=0
                        codes.append(code)
                        sizes.append(size)
                    if should_skip:
                        continue
                    if len(codes)==3 and len(set(codes))==1:
                        nf_code=codes[0]
                        uniq_sizes=len(set(sizes))
                        nf_size=sizes[0] if uniq_sizes==1 else None
                        if nf_code==404:
                            nf_size=None
                            info_msg=f"Detected nonexistent paths for {base_root} are (CODE:{nf_code})"
                        else:
                            if nf_size is not None:
                                info_msg=f"Detected nonexistent paths for {base_root} are (CODE:{nf_code}|SIZE:{nf_size})"
                            else:
                                info_msg=f"Detected nonexistent paths for {base_root} are (CODE:{nf_code})"
                        self.not_found_map[base_root]=(nf_code,nf_size)
                        if not self.silent:
                            print(f"[INFO] {info_msg}")
                    else:
                        self.not_found_map[base_root]=None
                    if base_root in error_counts and self.max_errors!=0 and error_counts[base_root]>=self.max_errors:
                        continue
            # split targets
            split=self.wordlist_split if self.wordlist_split>0 else 1
            chunks=[[] for _ in range(split)]
            for idx,w in enumerate(word_targets):
                chunks[idx % split].append(w)
            # filter empty chunks
            chunks=[c for c in chunks if c]
            # function to scan chunk
            new_dirs=[]
            lock_new=threading.Lock()
            def scan_chunk(chunk):
                if self.verbose>=1:
                    self.log_debug(f"Scanning {dir_url}")
                consecutive=0
                local_new=[]
                for word in chunk:
                    if self.throttle:
                        time.sleep(self.throttle/1000.0)
                    target=dir_url+word
                    self.log_trace(target)
                    code,size,hdrs,body,err=self.do_request(target, self.verb.upper())
                    if err:
                        with self.print_lock:
                            print(f"Curl error after requesting {target} : [7] Couldn't connect to server ({err})")
                        consecutive+=1
                        if self.max_errors!=0 and consecutive>=self.max_errors:
                            break
                        continue
                    else:
                        consecutive=0
                    is_dir=False
                    is_listable=False
                    redirect_url=""
                    dir_code=code
                    dir_size=size
                    dir_hdrs=hdrs
                    dir_body=body
                    dir_url_report=target
                    if code in (301,302):
                        loc=hdrs.get("Location") or hdrs.get("location")
                        if loc:
                            abs_loc=urljoin(target, loc)
                            try:
                                p_t=urlparse(target)
                                p_l=urlparse(abs_loc)
                                if p_l.path == p_t.path + "/":
                                    is_dir=True
                                    redirect_url=abs_loc
                                    slash_url=target+"/"
                                    self.log_trace(slash_url)
                                    code2,size2,hdrs2,body2,err2=self.do_request(slash_url, self.verb.upper())
                                    if err2:
                                        with self.print_lock:
                                            print(f"Curl error after requesting {slash_url} : [7] Couldn't connect to server ({err2})")
                                        continue
                                    dir_code=code2
                                    dir_size=size2
                                    dir_hdrs=hdrs2
                                    dir_body=body2
